findings.claim: An explicit `overlay apply --push` silently pushes nothing when the remote-tracking ref origin/main is absent (new or never-fetched origin): the entire push/notice block, including the --push branch, sits inside the `git rev-parse --verify -q origin/main` guard with no else path, so the documented contract 'Never pushes main unless --push' is silently violated on first delivery to a fresh remote — no push, no NOTICE, no error. cmd_capture handles the analogous missing-ref case with `git push -u origin upstream`, but cmd_apply has no `git push -u origin main` counterpart.
proof_refs: bin/labdrian-overlay:792 — the whole main push/notice block is gated by `if git rev-parse --verify -q origin/main >/dev/null; then` with no else branch, so an absent remote-tracking ref skips everything with zero output
bin/labdrian-overlay:796 — the user's explicit --push request (`push_main`) is only consulted inside that guard, so it is silently dropped when origin/main does not resolve
bin/labdrian-overlay:103 — the new help text promises 'Never pushes main unless --push', implying --push does push; the flag becoming a silent no-op contradicts the documented behavior

bin/labdrian-overlay:674 — contrast: cmd_capture's parallel logic handles the missing-remote-ref case explicitly with `git push -u origin upstream`, showing the missing else path in cmd_apply is an omission, not a design choice

findings.claim: cmd_capture now unconditionally pushes the upstream branch, turning a previously local-only operation into one that fails without a reachable origin: when no origin remote exists or the network is down, `git push -u origin upstream` (missing-ref path) or `git push origin upstream` errors, and under the script's apparent strict-error discipline capture aborts after the local sync commit (the pre-existing EXIT trap restores the branch, so state is preserved but the run reports failure). Offline capture is a regression relative to base behavior.
proof_refs: bin/labdrian-overlay:674 — `git push -u origin upstream` runs unconditionally whenever origin/upstream does not resolve, which includes the no-origin-remote and offline cases, not only the genuinely-new-remote-branch case
bin/labdrian-overlay:670 — the existing-ref path likewise issues a network push with no failure handling or offline tolerance
bin/labdrian-overlay:678 — the checkout back to the original branch is sequenced after the push, so a push failure exits via the trap rather than completing the documented 'Returned to branch' flow

findings.claim: When apply is started from a detached HEAD, `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` yields the literal string 'HEAD', so both the EXIT trap and the final restore execute `git checkout HEAD` — a no-op — and the session ends on main instead of the original commit, contradicting the new comment's own invariant that apply 'must never strand a session's checkout on main'. The trap additionally suppresses all checkout output and errors, so this restore failure mode is invisible to the user.
proof_refs: bin/labdrian-overlay:714 — `current_branch="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"` returns 'HEAD' on a detached checkout, capturing no restorable ref
bin/labdrian-overlay:719 — the trap runs `git checkout "$current_branch" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`, which for the literal value 'HEAD' succeeds as a no-op on main and hides any diagnostic
bin/labdrian-overlay:786 — the happy-path restore `git checkout "$current_branch"` has the same no-op behavior, then line 788 reports 'Returned to branch: HEAD' misleadingly

findings.claim: The candidate adds several externally observable behaviors — dirty-tree rejection in capture and apply, unconditional upstream auto-push with distinct existing-ref and first-push paths, --push gating of main, and the ahead-of-origin NOTICE — and the changed-path manifest contains no test asserting any of them, so every new branch of this delivery-critical sync logic ships unproved. The cheapest useful level is a shell test (e.g. bats) driving the script against a scratch git repo with a file:// origin, asserting: capture/apply die on a dirty tree, apply without --push leaves origin/main untouched and prints the NOTICE with the correct count, and apply --push advances origin/main.
proof_refs: bin/labdrian-overlay:700 — the new --push option introduces a behavioral fork (push vs. NOTICE) with no test exercising either side
bin/labdrian-overlay:586 — the capture dirty-tree guard's die path is asserted nowhere; a regression to its `--untracked-files=no` scoping would go undetected
bin/labdrian-overlay:668 — the upstream push has two distinct code paths (existing remote ref vs. `push -u` first push) whose selection logic is untested

findings.claim: Both new divergence checks compare against remote-tracking refs without fetching first, so on a multi-machine setup the ahead count in the NOTICE can misreport (origin/main stale since the last fetch) and the upstream/main pushes can fail non-fast-forward with only git's raw error as guidance; consider mentioning `sync-check --fetch` in the NOTICE or wrapping the pushes with a hint for the rejected-push case.
proof_refs: bin/labdrian-overlay:794 — `git rev-list --count origin/main..main` reads the local remote-tracking ref, which reflects the last fetch, not the remote's current state

bin/labdrian-overlay:669 — the upstream ahead check `git rev-list origin/upstream..upstream` has the same staleness, so a push can be attempted and rejected when another machine already advanced origin/upstream

evidence: Inspected the complete unified diff for bin/labdrian-overlay (blob 3d6d2b78 → b7f2111d, mode 100755 unchanged), the only path in the changed-path manifest; the review covers 100% of the candidate's changed paths.

Traced both modified command paths end to end: cmd_capture (dirty-tree guard at lines 584-588, unconditional upstream push with existing-ref and first-push branches at lines 666-676) and cmd_apply (--push parsing at lines 700-702, dirty-tree guard at lines 708-711, EXIT-trap branch restoration at lines 713-719, restore and main push/NOTICE block at lines 785-806), including failure ordering relative to the EXIT traps.
